# AGENTS.md

Rules and map for this repository, written for an agent starting cold. Read this,
then read the code. This file holds invariants only: if a fact can change without
anyone editing this file, it does not belong here.

## 1. Hierarchy

- `mind` (this repo) is the authority. This file governs work in `mind` and in
  every sibling repo reached from it.
- `cods` appears in §7 as a capability inventory, not a second rulebook. These
  rules apply when working there too; its own `AGENTS.md` is a three-line pointer
  back to this one, so an agent opened in that repo still finds the rules.
- Supervisory authority: `mind` inspects, audits and sets standards for the
  ecosystem, and may write the agent instruction files of subordinate projects. It
  does not own their runtime — deployment, source, data and enforcement stay with
  them. The full charter is `docs/MIND-AUTHORITY.md`.
- The code is the truth. When this file and the code disagree, say so and fix the
  file in the same change.

## 2. Hard rules

1. **Never deploy unless asked.** In this repo a push to `main` *is* a deploy:
   `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` runs `npm ci` → `npm test` → `npm run build` →
   `wrangler deploy`. Treat a push as a deploy. Cloudflare API writes, uploads and
   deletes are always off-limits without an explicit request.
2. **Brand identity — exact spelling and pronunciation.**
   - Emerging brand: `nspired.cc`. New brand architecture, new documentation and new
     interfaces use it. It is the direction of travel, not a settled replacement.
   - Current identity during the transition: `AI-Nspired` at `ai-nspired.com` — correct
     for today's prose and URLs, not permanently canonical. Do not present the old brand
     as the settled name, and do not retro-edit historical references.
   - Brand name: `AI-Nspired`
   - Pronunciation: “A-I inspired” — say A-I as two letters, then the word “inspired”.
   - Exact spelling: `AI-Nspired` — A-I, hyphen, Nspired. The hyphen is part of the name,
     not a separator you may move or drop.
   - One string, three capitalisations: `AI-Nspired`, `ai-Nspired`, `ai-nspired`.
     Same letters, same hyphen, only case differs; `ai-nspired.com` is the
     all-lowercase form of `AI-Nspired` — one string, never re-hyphenated, never a
     different word.
   - Primary domain: `ai-nspired.com` — current; legacy during the transition.
   - Use `AI-Nspired` in prose and branding; use lowercase `ai-nspired.com` in URLs.
   - Never substitute `Inspired`, `AI Inspired`, or `AI-Inspired` for the brand name:
     those are different letters, so they name a different word.
   - Preserve this spelling in generated documentation, interfaces, metadata,
     prompts, agent responses, and speech-oriented output.
   - This rule does not rename the product: `ai-Ncards` is the product name today,
     and its relationship to `nspired.cc` is a separate product-naming decision.
3. **Do not create workers.** The account already has more than it needs; fix the
   ones that exist. `PROJECTS.md` has the current count and never drifts.
4. **Ask before changing code or stored data.** One question, then continue. Do not
   hand a decision back as a menu of options, and do not make an assumption in
   place of a question.
5. **Dictation is free for everyone, forever.** No plan check, no key, no login, in
   either repo.
6. **Never grade or critique the owner's legal or methodological output.** He is
   the method.
7. **Secrets by name only** — `CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN`, `CLOUDFLARE_ACCOUNT_ID`,
   `GITHUB_PAT`, `OPENROUTER_API_KEY`, `ADMIN_KEY`. Never echo a value, never write
   one into a file, command or reply.
8. **Model roles are decisions, not options.** §6. If a named model is unavailable,
   stop and ask. Never substitute a llama model for one of them.
9. **Verify before claiming.** Run the check; report failures as failures. Never
   loosen an assertion to make a change pass — if the behaviour changed on purpose,
   rename the expectation.

## 3. What this repo is

`mind` is a flip-card AI chat on Cloudflare Workers: the front end in `public/` and
the API in `src/` are served from one origin (no CORS), answers arrive as cards, and
knowledge is layered — the separate `truth` worker owns curated truth, `mind`
answers from it first and saves everything it produces as a candidate.

## 4. Verify

```bash
npm ci          # dependencies are not preserved between sessions
npm run check   # node --check over every source file, including public/script.js
npm run build   # wrangler deploy --dry-run: bundling and bindings, deploys nothing
```

A green `check` and `build` is the floor, not proof: neither exercises the network,
the browser or a real deploy. Say what was verified and what was only read.

## 5. Map

| path | what lives there |
| --- | --- |
| `src/index.js` | worker entry, route table, chat pipeline |
| `src/decide.js` | clef decision ladder, decision cache |
| `src/engine.js` | model calls and timeouts |
| `src/truth.js` | truth layers, `promote()`, TTLs, candidates |
| `src/bindings.js` | which binding a store resolves to |
| `src/admin.js` | read-only admin API (`/api/admin/*`) |
| `src/providers/` | `workers-ai.js`, `openrouter.js` |
| `src/audio.js`, `extract.js`, `shot.js`, `sessions.js` | ASR slicing, attachments, screenshots, login state |
| `public/script.js` | the app |
| `public/admin.html` | the console at `/admin` |
| `test.mjs` | all tests |
| `PROJECTS.md` | every Worker and repo, plus which of them have README/AGENTS — generated, never hand-edited |
| `scripts/overview.mjs` | rebuilds `PROJECTS.md` from the account and GitHub |
| `docs/JUSTICE-ECOSYSTEM-BASELINE.md` | what the `justice` Worker and its four resources actually are — bindings, IDs, auth, gaps — confirmed read-only |
| `docs/JUSTICE-ARCHITECTURE.md` | the target EITL architecture, with §9 measuring it against the deployed system |
| `docs/MIND-AUTHORITY.md` | what `mind` may do to subordinate projects and what it may not — inspection and instruction, never their runtime |
| `docs/EZ-EXHIBITZ-OWNER-ENTITLEMENT.md` | the instruction for that project's owner tier: role apart from plan, server-side credential, no IP recognition |

## 6. Data and bindings

| binding | kind | target |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ASSETS` | assets | `./public` |
| `AI` | Workers AI | vision, whisper, clef ladder |
| `BROWSER` | Browser Rendering | `/api/shot`, one page per shot |
| `BUCKET` | R2 | `r2-explorer-bucket` |
| `SESSIONS` | Durable Object | one per user, sqlite, migration tag `v1` |
| `MEM` | KV | `4a9bfbffb4d440cba86badc508e2045a` |
| `MASTER` | KV | `904eff3af4c14f06964e4f651cce9573` |
| `TEP` | Secrets Store | `7073bd5852014f83875874ae3ff0817e` / `TRUTH_ENGINE_PROMPT` |
| `TRUTH` | service | worker `truth` |

The same namespaces are bound under different names elsewhere. That is why an edit
in one place shows up in another:

- `904eff3a…` = `MASTER` (mind) = `TRUTHS` (cods) = `MASTER_TRUTHS` (truth worker)
- `4a9bfbff…` = `MEM` (mind, Memoria) = `PROV_TRUTH` (truth worker)

Truth worker facts that matter here: master records are written with **no TTL**,
provisional records carry a **24-hour** TTL, and all six write routes require
`ADMIN_KEY` in `x-admin-key`. Reads (`/api/truth/resolve`, `/debug/kv-status`) are
public. The console's Save writes master through that gate
(`public/admin.html`), so it must send the key.

Do not align the two `ADMIN_KEY`s to make a test pass. They are separate secrets on
purpose: `mind`'s key governs the console and its read API, the truth worker's governs
writes to stored truth, and holding one is not holding the other.

## 7. Sibling repo `cods`

Capability inventory, not policy. Read its code before changing it; these notes come
from its 2026-10-31 handoff.

- A second card app that solves the same problem differently. Worker `cods`, repo
  `dno-luigi/cods`, catalogued by `tools/build-catalogue.mjs`.
- `POST /stt` — free dictation, no key, 8 MB cap, 120 clips per address per day,
  both models and both shapes tried.
- Truth path: `truthStore()` prefers `TRUTHS` → `ARCHIVE` → `KV`; every answer is
  stored as a candidate with confidence 0.4–0.85; `POST /truths/<id>/approve` with
  `x-truth-key` promotes to master at 0.9; `GET /truths?status=candidate` lists.
- OpenRouter work: `openRouterCall()` returns `{text, citations}`; `OR_WEB_PLUGIN`
  grounds the main call only, so card sub-calls do not pay for a search.
  `use_web:false` opts out.
- Tools: `tools/pull-worker.mjs <name> [outDir]` pulls a deployed worker read-only.
- Checks: `npm run check`, `npm test` (`node test.mjs`).

## 8. Open conflicts — fix, do not copy

1. **llama.** The rule forbids llama in any ladder or picker, but `mind` still
   names it twice: `src/index.js:69` and `src/index.js:73`, plus
   `src/providers/workers-ai.js:16`. `cods` documents llama-3.2-1b in
   `CF_TEXT_MODELS`. Either the rule or those entries is wrong; resolve before
   adding more.
2. **DeepSeek id.** `mind` uses `@cf/deepseek-ai/deepseek-v4.1-flash-1017`; the
   `cods` doc says `deepseek-v4-flash-0731`. One id is canonical; the other is drift.
3. **The truth worker's gate** is enforced today (`adminGated: true`). Older notes
   describing those routes as open are stale.

4. **Save and erase share one key inside the truth worker.** `adminRequired` compares a
   single `ADMIN_KEY` against every path in `ADMIN_WRITE_PATHS` — create, update, delete
   and promote — so the least-privilege split exists between the two workers, not inside
   the truth worker. That function also returns unguarded when `ADMIN_KEY` is unset,
   where `mind`'s `adminGate` fails closed with 503. Decide whether erase and promotion
   each need their own key before calling the split done.

## 9. Stop and ask

- The change is irreversible, or it touches stored truth, KV or R2 contents.
- It needs a deploy or a push to `main`.
- It would create a worker, or change a binding or namespace.
- A named model is unavailable, or a check fails for a reason you cannot explain.
- Two instructions conflict, or this file disagrees with the code.

## 10. Maintaining this file

Invariants only, one line each, no line numbers, no counts that drift, no open
questions (those belong in `HANDOFF.md`). Delete a rule when it stops being true —
a stale rule is worse than no rule.

# AA — Integration Contract

**Status:** draft v1, for review. Nothing in this document is implemented, and no
application is conforming.
**Date:** 2026-11-18
**Scope:** ARA (reasoning authority) · AA (interaction, context and integration
layer) · host applications, of which `mind` is the first.
**Authoritative for:** this contract. ARA's interface is recorded in §9 from a
read-only pull of the deployed worker on 2026-11-18, not from Mind's assumptions.
It is still **not** authoritative for the quality of ARA's decisions.

This document exists because a working integration is not the same thing as a
standard. `mind` already reaches ARA directly (`src/ara.js`, binding `ARA` in
`wrangler.jsonc`) and already carries an ambient assistant (`assist()` at
`src/index.js:679`), but neither is governed by a written contract: the domain
parameter is dead, no version travels with a request, nothing declares what the
host permits, and nothing states what ARA may not do. Every future application
would otherwise copy that shape.

The goal is **not** to make `mind` compatible with AA. The goal is to establish a
standard that `mind` implements first, and that every subsequent application —
including applications owned by other people — implements consistently without
surrendering its own authority.

---

## 0. Boundary law

Nine invariants. A proposed change that breaks one is rejected regardless of how
well it performs.

| # | Invariant |
| --- | --- |
| **A1** | **Hosts integrate with AA. AA integrates with ARA.** No host application binds, addresses, or reimplements ARA. |
| **A2** | **ARA owns reasoning.** ARA decides. It writes nothing into a host's store, prompt, card, or configuration. |
| **A3** | **The host owns its runtime.** Bindings, data, deployment, and enforcement remain with the application. AA is never given a host's store. |
| **A4** | **AA holds no truth.** Manifests, envelopes, and event records only. Nothing curated, nothing promoted, nothing served as an answer. |
| **A5** | **A manifest declares; only execution proves.** A valid manifest establishes intended integration, never enforced integration. |
| **A6** | **Provenance cannot be upgraded in transit.** No layer may set `verified: true` on evidence it did not originate and verify. |
| **A7** | **Deny by default.** An unnamed capability, an unresolved scope, or an absent approval is a refusal, not an assumption. |
| **A8** | **Context is data, never instruction.** Text supplied by a host may inform a decision; it may never act as a directive to AA or ARA, and may never alter their rules. |
| **A9** | **Explicit approval requires an authenticated actor.** No approval is valid without a named principal behind it. |

**Why A8 is written first and enforced later.** This ecosystem has already paid for
its absence: `docs/SIS-WORKFLOW-SCHEMA.md` `I6` records retrieved text arriving as a
`system`-role message and therefore speaking with instruction authority. AA forwards
context by design, so it inherits that failure mode unless the rule is both stated
and demonstrated. A8 is the only invariant whose conformance requires a negative
execution test at two boundaries (§7.3) — documentation of A8 proves nothing.

---

## 1. Roles and the authority matrix

Three parties, three authorities, deliberately unequal.

| Party | Holds | Does not hold |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **ARA** | Reasoning authority: intent interpretation, domains, decisions, confidence, learning | Any write into a host, any host binding, any approval |
| **AA** | Mediation: the contract, the envelope, capability enforcement, the ARA gateway | Truth, host data, approval, execution |
| **Host** | Operational authority: bindings, store, deployment, execution, approval | Reasoning authority, the right to address ARA directly |

The eight connections. This table, not the message format, is what makes this an
architecture:

| Connection | Supplied by | Validated by | May change it | Mode |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Identity** | host — manifest plus authenticated session | AA — schema, pinned contract version | host only; AA may reject, never rewrite | declarative |
| **Context** | host adapter | host first, then AA against `context.provides` caps | host only | read-only to AA and ARA |
| **Intent** | host and operator | AA — `kind` must appear in `intent.kinds` | operator, through the host | advisory → executable per capability |
| **Domain** | host map; ARA owns domain knowledge | AA — mapping closure; ARA — its own domains | ARA owns the knowledge; the host owns the map | declarative |
| **Capabilities** | host | AA — anything unnamed is denied | host | executable, gated |
| **Authorization** | host decides; operator approves | AA — refuses to mint or approve | operator only | gate |
| **Feedback** | operator → host → AA → ARA | AA — kind; host — actor | ARA may learn; host records | write |
| **Provenance** | host (origin); ARA (truth layer) | AA — no upgrade, ever | the originating party only | immutable once sent |

Reading the table left to right: **who supplies** it, **who validates** it, **who
may change** it, and **whether it is read-only, advisory, or executable**. A
connection that cannot fill all five columns is not integrated; it is a shared
message shape.

---

## 2. The envelope

Two version identifiers, deliberately separate:

- **Wire version** — `aa-contract/1` — names the envelope. It is what a request or a
  response carries, and it changes only when a field, a required input, or a message
  semantic changes.
- **Document revision** — `1.2` today — names this text. It changes when the
  specification is clarified, a conformance rule is tightened, or evidence changes,
  and it does not touch the wire.

A change that adds a required field or alters a semantic bumps the wire version.
Adding an optional field, clarifying a rule, or restating where evidence is kept
bumps only the revision. Both are recorded under Document revisions, so the two
numbers cannot be confused for one another.

### 2.1 Request

```json
{
  "contract": "aa-contract/1",
  "id": "01JC9Z6Q7R5F3M2X8K4B1N0P",
  "sentAt": "2026-11-18T14:02:11.418Z",
  "identity": {
    "app": "mind",
    "environment": "production",
    "surface": "card-board",
    "adapter": "in-process"
  },
  "intent": { "kind": "ask", "text": "…", "choice": null },
  "domain": { "name": "mind.cards", "from": ["canvas.cards", "card.selection"] },
  "context": [
    {
      "slice": "canvas.cards",
      "chars": 8321,
      "provenance": {
        "ref": "mind:canvas.cards",
        "suppliedBy": "host",
        "observedAt": "2026-11-18T14:02:11.401Z",
        "verified": false,
        "verifiedBy": null,
        "layer": null,
        "correlation": { "ray": null }
      }
    }
  ],
  "capabilities": ["cards.read", "canvas.render"],
  "approval": null
}
```

`identity.adapter` is `in-process` or `service`. It is normative: it must appear in
every envelope, every log record derived from one, and every health response, so
that no artefact — code comment, README, or review record — can describe the
migration seam as the shared service.

### 2.2 Response

```json
{
  "contract": "aa-contract/1",
  "id": "01JC9Z6Q7R5F3M2X8K4B1N0P",
  "decision": {
    "move": "answer",
    "route": "generate",
    "clarify": null,
    "notes": []
  },
  "authority": {
    "writes": [],
    "requested": ["cards.read"],
    "refused": []
  },
  "provenance": [],
  "notes": []
}
```

`authority` is not decoration. It states what ARA believes it was permitted to do
(`writes` is always empty under A2) and what it asked the host for. A response whose
`authority.writes` is non-empty is a contract violation and must be refused by AA.

---

## 3. Capability semantics

A capability is a named, bounded permission declared by the host. It carries three
independent attributes, and no attribute implies another.

| Attribute | Values | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `ops` | `read` · `advisory` · `execute` | an explicit set; membership is exact, with no wildcard and no implication |
| `scope` | `session` · `app` · `owner` | who the capability is valid for; resolved by the host, never asserted by the caller |
| `approval` | `none` · `explicit` | a third gate, not a flag on the first |

`read` permits observation. `advisory` permits AA or ARA to *recommend* an action
that the host performs. `execute` permits a request to change state, and is always
gated. A capability declared `read` must never pass an `execute` check; that
inversion was present in an earlier draft of this standard and is the reason the
table above names the three modes explicitly.

### 3.1 Declared form

```json
{ "id": "cards.read",    "ops": ["read"],     "scope": "session" }
{ "id": "canvas.render", "ops": ["advisory"], "scope": "session" }
{ "id": "truth.purge",   "ops": ["execute"],  "scope": "owner", "approval": "explicit" }
{ "id": "engine.switch", "ops": ["execute"],  "scope": "owner", "approval": "explicit" }
```

These four are `mind`'s **proposed** set. They are not attached to any manifest that
exists (see §10), and two of them correspond to routes that are already gated today
(`/api/truth/purge`, `POST /api/engine`), which is what makes them the natural
first capabilities rather than invented ones.

### 3.2 Rules

1. A capability not named in the manifest does not exist. There is no default grant.
2. `ops` is matched exactly. There is no hierarchy in which `read` subsumes
   `advisory` or `execute`.
3. `scope` is resolved by the host from its own authenticated session. A caller may
   request a scope; the request carries no weight.
4. `approval: "explicit"` is enforced at gate three (§4), never at gate one.
5. A capability that an integration cannot enforce is not declared. Declaring it
   and relying on good intentions violates A5.

---

## 4. Authorization

Three gates in series. Each fails closed, and failure is a refusal — never a
degraded grant.

```
gate 1  capability known and op ∈ ops      → else  capability_unknown
gate 2  scope satisfied by the actor       → else  scope_denied
gate 3  approval valid for {cap, actor}    → else  approval_required
```

### 4.1 The actor

The actor is resolved by the host from its own session, before AA is called. In
`mind` that machinery already exists and is named here so an implementer does not
invent a second one:

| Purpose | Existing code |
| --- | --- |
| Read the token's account | `src/sessions.js` `tokenUser()`, `readSession()` |
| Resolve the request to a user | `src/index.js` `sessionUser()` |
| Constant-time key comparison | `src/util.js` `keyMatches()` — length checked, then XOR |
| Fail-closed admin gate | `src/admin.js` `adminGate()` — `503 admin_key_unset` |
| Fail-closed engine gate | `src/index.js` `keyGate()` — `503 key_unset` |

`actor` is a named account or `null`. `null` is legal for ordinary reads and is
never legal for approval (A9).

### 4.2 The approval

An approval is a host-minted, single-use token bound to a specific capability and a
specific actor.

| Property | Requirement |
| --- | --- |
| Minted by | the host, using a secret it already holds for its execute gates (`ADMIN_KEY` in `mind`) |
| Bound to | `{ capability, actor }` — a token for `truth.purge` is not a token for `engine.switch` |
| Lifetime | short; 60 seconds is the ceiling |
| Reuse | single-use; replay is refused |
| Visible to | AA and the host only. **ARA never receives one** |
| Comparison | constant-time (`keyMatches`) |

AA cannot mint an approval, cannot widen one, and cannot treat a request containing
`approval: "explicit"` as evidence that approval occurred. Only a valid token
satisfies gate three.

### 4.3 Fail-closed behaviour and the legacy override

**Decision D1.** Explicit approval requires an authenticated actor. With
`LOGIN_PASSWORD` unset, an `execute` capability is `unavailable` — refused, not
granted — because there is nobody to name.

This narrows behaviour that exists today. `src/index.js` currently allows
`body.override` to proceed anonymously when login is not configured, and records
`override:<timestamp>` in `MEM` with `actor: "anonymous"`. That path predates this
contract. It is recorded here as **legacy**, it is **not** part of the AA
authorization model, and it must not be extended to any new capability. Reconciling
it — either by requiring a named actor for overrides or by retiring the path — is
an open decision, not a settled exception.

---

## 5. Provenance

Provenance is a claim with an owner and a verification state. It is not a proof, and
no field in it may be manufactured.

### 5.1 Record

```json
{
  "ref": "mind:canvas.cards",
  "suppliedBy": "host",
  "observedAt": "2026-11-18T14:02:11.401Z",
  "verified": false,
  "verifiedBy": null,
  "layer": null,
  "correlation": { "ray": null }
}
```

### 5.2 Rules

1. `verified: true` requires `verifiedBy` to name the party that verified it, and
   that party must be the one that originated the material.
2. AA may never set `verified` or `verifiedBy`. It carries them or refuses the
   envelope.
3. `correlation` holds request identifiers — a Cloudflare ray id, a host request id.
   It is a correlation aid, **not** identity, **not** proof of source, and never a
   substitute for `verifiedBy`. An earlier draft of this standard proposed a ray id
   as provenance; that was wrong and is recorded here so it is not reintroduced.
4. `layer` is `master`, `provisional`, `candidate`, or `null`, and is set only for
   material derived from a truth store.
5. Truth-derived material reuses the field that already exists:
   `origin: { source, verified, created, fresh }` from `src/truth.js`
   `resolveRemoteTruth()`. The contract does not introduce a second vocabulary for
   the same fact.
6. Provenance is immutable once sent. A downstream party may append a record; it
   may not amend one.

---

## 6. Feedback

Three kinds, each carrying its actor, each returning to the reasoning foundation
through AA.

| Kind | Produced by | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `verdict` | operator | a decision was correct, or was corrected to something else |
| `correction` | operator | the content, not the routing, was wrong |
| `preference` | operator | how this kind of ask should be handled next time |

**Requirement R-F1:** the host records feedback locally *before or regardless of*
ARA's reachability, and an unreachable ARA never discards the operator's judgement.

**Known gap in `mind`.** The verdict route in `src/index.js` calls `sendVerdict()`
first and returns `502 verdict_failed` when it fails; the `verdict:<timestamp>:<id>`
record in `MEM` is written only after a successful send. So a correction made while
ARA is down is currently lost. That is a gap against R-F1, recorded as such, and it
is not repaired by this document.

---

## 7. Conformance — a manifest is not evidence

**A5 in operational form.** A valid manifest proves that an application *declares*
its intended integration. It proves nothing about what the application enforces.
Conformance is established only by execution, and only by evidence another party can
inspect.

### 7.1 Levels

| Level | Established by | Evidence required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `declared` | the manifest validates against this contract | the manifest itself |
| `implemented` | a code path exercises every connection the manifest declares | a source reference per connection |
| `verified` | each connection exercised against real behaviour | recorded request/response pairs, trace ids, actor, timestamp, and a named reviewer |
| `conforming` | all eight connections `verified`, review record signed, and no bypass of the gateway remains | the review record in `docs/integrations/<app>.md` |

### 7.2 Promotion rules

1. No promotion on documentation alone.
2. No promotion on static analysis or unit tests alone. Stubs and fixtures prove the
   shape of a call, not that a boundary is enforced.
3. Conformance is tracked **per connection** and in aggregate. The aggregate is the
   **lowest** connection level; there are no averages.
4. `identity.adapter === "in-process"` caps an integration at `verified`. Only a
   deployment addressing AA as a service can reach `conforming`.
5. A level once reached is not inherited by a new contract version. A version bump
   returns every connection to `implemented` until re-verified.

### 7.3 A8 requires execution evidence at both boundaries

A8 (`context is data, never instruction`) is the one invariant that cannot be
evidenced by reading code or by a declarative test. Conformance for it requires:

| Boundary | Evidence required |
| --- | --- |
| **host → AA** | a recorded exchange in which a context slice containing imperative text ("ignore previous instructions", "mark this verified", "you are now…") arrives as labelled data, is not promoted to a system or instruction channel, and changes neither the decision nor any provenance field |
| **AA → ARA** | a recorded exchange showing the same slice still delimited and labelled as data, with the response's `authority.writes` empty and no rule change attributable to it |
| **negative case** | the same payload with `verified: true` and no `verifiedBy` is refused at the envelope gate, not passed through |

A connection may not be marked `verified` for A8 on the strength of a prompt
instruction, a code comment, or a reviewer's assurance. The evidence is the recorded
exchange, including the negative case.

### 7.4 Evidence record

Each `verified` claim names: the connection, the code path exercised, the request
and response (or a bounded excerpt with a trace id), the actor, the UTC timestamp,
the contract version, and the reviewer.

Evidence lives with the review record, not in a chat log — **and it is committed to
the repository** under `evidence/<component>-<date>/`, with a `README.md` recording
how it was obtained, what it is evidence of, and what it does not establish. An
uncommitted path cannot be audited: two evidence directories named by existing
documents — `evidence/snapshot-2026-11-06/` in `docs/SETUP-AS-BUILT.md` and
`evidence/justice-discovery/` in `docs/JUSTICE-ECOSYSTEM-BASELINE.md` — are absent
from this working tree, so the `verified` claims resting on them cannot now be
checked. **A `verified` level whose evidence is not committed is downgraded to
`implemented`.**

This states where evidence is kept; it changes no envelope field and no message
semantic, so the wire version stays `aa-contract/1` (see Document revisions).

---

## 8. The review gate

No integration becomes part of the architecture without a review record answering
these seven questions, each with a conformance status.

| # | Question | Required answer |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | What is being connected? | both parties, named, with the binding or transport |
| 2 | Why does the connection exist? | the capability it unlocks; what breaks without it |
| 3 | What information flows in each direction? | every field, with caps and redactions |
| 4 | What authority does each participant retain? | stated against §1, including what each may refuse |
| 5 | What can be read, written, or executed? | one line per capability, using §3 vocabulary |
| 6 | How is it authenticated and verified? | actor resolution, approval, and the evidence under §7 |
| 7 | How does it preserve the architecture? | confirmation that no host addresses ARA and AA holds no truth (A1, A4) |

The record's status uses §7.1 vocabulary only. A record claiming `conforming` while
any connection is `implemented` is itself a defect.

---

## 9. The ARA boundary — confirmed by pull, 2026-11-18

**Decision D2, completed.** The contract was written first (§0–§8) with ARA
recorded as `client-observed`. The deployed worker has since been pulled read-only
and reconciled. What follows is the deployed interface; where it and Mind's client
disagree, the deployed worker wins and this document is corrected.

**Method, and what it is evidence of.** `GET /accounts/…/workers/scripts/ara`
returned the bundle (67,876 bytes, one ES module, 2,040 lines, `node --check`
clean), `…/scripts/ara/settings` returned the bindings, and three unauthenticated
`GET` probes recorded live responses. **No `POST` was sent, nothing was written,
nothing deployed.** Evidence: `evidence/ara-discovery/`.

**Deployment facts.** Bundle `last-modified` **2026-11-18 04:17:36 UTC**, etag
`a98ddb88…2242`, compatibility date **2025-07-01**. That is newer than
`PROJECTS.md` (2026-11-09) and newer than Mind's client, so this section records
what runs now, not what shipped in September.

### 9.1 The deployed interface

| Route | Method | Auth | Behaviour |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `/health` | GET | none | `{"status":"ok","kv":true,"latencyMs":0}` — probed 200 |
| `/decide` | POST | none | the decision path (§9.2) |
| `/outcome` | POST | `x-admin-key` | records what the decision produced |
| `/feedback` | POST | `x-admin-key` | records a verdict |
| `/recent` | GET | `x-admin-key` | recent decisions, by domain |
| `/domains` | GET | none | domain records with counts and move histograms — probed 200 |
| `/domains` | POST | `x-admin-key` | registers a domain |
| `/review` | GET | none | learned review text for a domain and ask |
| `/progress` | GET | none | progress by domain |
| `/resolve` | POST | none | a separate research and generation path, with web search and an ethics filter |
| anything else | any | none | `ara-engine-active` — probed 200 |

`adminGate` compares `x-admin-key` in constant time, accepts no bearer form, and
fails closed with `503 admin_not_configured` when its `ADMIN_KEY` is unset. It is
the same shape as Mind's gate, and the opposite of the truth worker's unguarded
fall-through recorded in `AGENTS.md` §8.

Mind's client timeouts remain as implemented: 8s on `/decide`, 2s on `/outcome`,
3s on `/feedback`.

### 9.2 What `/decide` actually does

Request read: `text` (or `prompt`), `domain`, `surface`, `choice` → `forced`,
`stored`. Response, from `arrive()`:

```text
{ id, key, at, domain, surface, move, route, refused, cost, reviewed, idiom,
  consensus, notes, question, options }
```

plus either `clarify: { text, questions: [{ id, q, options: [{ value, label }] }] }`
or — for a held pair that asks back instead of answering — `answer` alongside
`clarify`.

Six behaviours the contract must record, because Mind's client assumes otherwise:

1. **`surface` selects the vocabulary.** `SURFACES` defines `mind` and `cards`,
each with its own question, move labels and store. The `mind` face's moves are
`result`, `preset`, `ask`, `unclear`; the generic `MOVES` set is `card`, `template`,
`document`, `microsite`, `question`, `none`. A move means nothing without the
surface that produced it.
2. **`domain` must already be registered.** Selection is
`the decision's scope if known, else your domain if registered, else choices[0]`,
over the domains the worker tracks. `/domains` reports exactly one: `general`.
3. **`stored` is read before deciding**, and a held pair can produce a `clarify`
card instead of an answer.
4. **Every decision is written twice**: a row in D1 `decisions` (`at`, `domain`,
`asked`, `decided`, `correct`, `corrected_to`, `idiom`, `surface`, `model`, `cost`,
`ms`, `confidence`) and a KV key `int:<…>` with metadata capped at 1 KB.
5. **Reasoning runs on OpenRouter** (`JOINT_DECIDER`, `DECISIONS_URL`). The worker
has **no `AI` binding** at all.
6. **`notes` is ARA's own learned review text**, returned with the decision.

### 9.3 Divergences between Mind's client and the deployed worker

| # | Mind does | ARA does | Consequence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | sends `domain: 'mind'` (hardcoded in `askAra`) | keeps it only if registered, else `choices[0]` | every Mind decision is recorded under `general`; the domain claim is silently discarded. **This is the Domain defect, and it is Mind's, not ARA's** |
| 2 | sends `surface: 'mind'` | selects `SURFACES.mind` | **correct and load-bearing** — the only reason the move set is Mind's |
| 3 | maps `move` → preset: `result→truth`, `preset→operator`, `ask→operator` | emits exactly those moves on the mind face | coherent; `unclear` reaches Mind as a clarify card before the mapping is used |
| 4 | sends `route: decision.task` to `/outcome` | stores it beside its own `decided.route` | harmless, but two vocabularies now share one field name |
| 5 | treats `refused` or a missing `move` as failure | returns `refused: false` with `move: 'unclear'` + `clarify` | Mind's failure path is unreachable for the ordinary "unsure" case — right outcome, different route |
| 6 | discards ARA's `notes` (counts them only) | returns learned text with every decision | the learning round trip is one-way in practice, which is a Feedback failure, not a transport one |
| 7 | authenticates the journal with `ARA_KEY \|\| ADMIN_KEY` | accepts only its own `ADMIN_KEY` | if Mind's `ARA_KEY` is set and differs, every outcome and verdict is 401 → `sendVerdict` false → `/api/truth/verdict` answers 502. A configuration fact that cannot be settled from the bundle; a check to perform, not a claim |

### 9.4 Findings that belong to ARA, not to Mind

One distinction first, because it was blurred in an earlier draft and matters:
**A1 governs the integration boundary** — which party a host application may call.
**ARA's own public surface is a separate control.** A host that never mentions ARA
still leaves the reasoning foundation exposed if anyone on the internet can call it
directly. Both need remediating; they are not the same defect, and fixing one does
not fix the other.

| Finding | Evidence | Why the contract cares |
| --- | --- | --- |
| five routes are reachable from the public internet unauthenticated: `POST /decide`, `POST /resolve`, `GET /domains`, `GET /review`, `GET /progress` | router lines and live probes | **a security defect in ARA, distinct from A1.** A1 governs who a host may call; this governs who may call ARA at all. `/resolve` runs a generation path on the owner's OpenRouter key, and routing every host through AA does not close it |
| `/domains` publishes the decision histogram — 364 decisions with per-move counts and `last` | probed body | domain inventory and operator behaviour are public |
| ARA holds `MIND`, `CODS`, `MASTER_TRUTHS`, `BROWSER`, `R2` and `CLOUDFLARE_ID` bindings its code never references — 0 occurrences of each in the bundle | settings plus a token scan | ARA is granted a service binding **into Mind**. It does not use it, so A2 holds at runtime today; but the channel exists without review, which offends A3 |
| ARA does not read `MASTER_TRUTHS` despite being bound to it | 0 occurrences | ARA's reasoning is not grounded in curated truth; the host supplies a stored pair via `stored`. That is a coordination decision which should be named, not left implicit |
| no contract version, no identity envelope, no `authority` block | response shape | ARA cannot distinguish a standard from a caller, and cannot state what it was permitted to do |

### 9.5 State of the reconciliation

**Done:** the interface is confirmed, the shapes are recorded, and §9.1–§9.4 replace
Mind's assumptions. Corrected in this document: the status line, this section, the
Domain row in §10, and D2/D3 in §11.

**Still open, in order:**

1. the `ARA_KEY` / `ADMIN_KEY` check in §9.3 row 7;
2. whether ARA keeps the `MIND` and `MASTER_TRUTHS` bindings — an ARA decision, not
   this document's;
3. whether the five unauthenticated routes are acceptable while AA does not exist;
4. D3's fix, which is now defined rather than guessed (§11).

`ara.verified` may be `true` for the **shape** of the interface — `/decide` in,
`/decide` out — and stays `false` for anything about the **quality** of a decision.

---

## 10. Mind's status today — the baseline

`mind` has **no manifest**, so it sits **below `declared`**. The nearest artefacts
are `src/ara.js` and the ambient assistant. This table is the baseline that later
evidence has to beat; nothing here is a conformance claim.

| Connection | Status | Where it stands today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | partial | `surface: 'mind'` is hardcoded in `src/ara.js` and is load-bearing — it selects ARA's mind face (§9.2). No environment, no adapter flag, no contract version travel with it |
| Context | partial | `assist()` sends one free-text field, `context`, capped at 12,000 characters; no slices, no caps, no provenance |
| Intent | partial | `{ text, choice, stored }`; no `kind`, no version; the move vocabulary is ARA's surface vocabulary, not a contract field |
| Domain | — | `domain` is hardcoded to `'mind'`, which ARA does not track, so every decision is recorded under `general` (§9.3 row 1) |
| Capabilities | — | none declared; two execute routes are gated but undeclared as capabilities |
| Authorization | partial | `adminGate`/`keyGate` fail closed; no approval token, no scope model; the anonymous `override` path is legacy (§4.3) |
| Feedback | partial | `sendVerdict()` and the `verdict:*` record exist; R-F1 is not met (§6) |
| Provenance | partial | `origin: { source, verified, created, fresh }` exists in `src/truth.js`; it does not travel as a required field |

Aggregate: **below `declared`.** The honest sentence is "`mind` reaches ARA
directly and carries an ambient assistant; it does not yet implement the contract."

One invariant is already true at runtime, and can be shown rather than asserted:
**A2 holds** — the deployed ARA holds a `MIND` service binding and references it
zero times, so nothing in ARA writes into this host (§9.4).

---

## 11. Decisions and deferrals

| # | Decision | Consequence in this document |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **D1** | Approval fails closed when `LOGIN_PASSWORD` is unset; explicit approval requires an authenticated actor; the existing anonymous override is preserved as documented legacy, never extended | §4.3 |
| **D2** | **Done 2026-11-18.** Contract first, then a read-only pull of the deployed worker and a reconciliation. ARA's interface is confirmed, not assumed from Mind's client | §9 |
| **D3** | **Traced 2026-11-18.** ARA collapses an unregistered domain to `general`; `surface` carries the vocabulary. The fix is now a choice, not a guess: send `general` (no write), or register the domain with the gated `POST /domains` (a write into ARA, which needs explicit approval) | §9.2, §9.3, §10 |

**D3 in one sentence:** a newly interpreted domain value must not be sent to an
unverified endpoint. The defect is documented and stays open; it is not quietly
fixed by guessing.

---

## 12. What this document does not do

- It changes no code, no binding, no deployment, and no stored record.
- It asserts ARA's interface only where §9 records a read-only pull or a probe, and
  nothing about the quality of its decisions.
- It does not repair what §9.4 found. The unauthenticated routes, ARA's unused
  `MIND` binding, and Mind's discarded `notes` are recorded findings, not changes.
- It does not make `mind` conforming, or `declared`, or implemented.
- It does not create the shared AA service. Until that service exists and an
  integration addresses it, every integration reports `adapter: in-process` and is
  capped at `verified` (§7.2 rule 4).
- It does not grant any application access to ARA or to a shared truth store. Hosts
  connect to AA; AA mediates with ARA; each host keeps its own operational
  authority. That is the whole point of writing this down.

---

## Document revisions

| Rev | Date | Change | Wire version |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 2026-11-18 | First issue: §0–§12, with ARA recorded `client-observed` | `aa-contract/1` |
| 1.1 | 2026-11-18 | §9 replaced with the confirmed interface from a read-only pull; §9.4 separates the integration boundary (A1) from ARA's public-surface defect; §7.4 requires evidence to be committed and downgrades an unbacked `verified` claim to `implemented` | `aa-contract/1` — unchanged |
| 1.2 | 2026-11-18 | §2 states the wire version and the document revision as separate identifiers, so a clarification cannot be mistaken for a change to the envelope (IA-5) | `aa-contract/1` — unchanged |

**Version discipline.** `aa-contract/1` names the envelope. §7.2 rule 5 returns
connections to `implemented` when that wire version changes. Revisions 1.1 and 1.2
change documentation and the evidence rule only, so they promote and demote nothing;
and because no connection currently stands above `below declared`, nothing is reset
either. A change to a field, a required input, or a message semantic is what bumps
the wire version — and would be recorded here as rev 2.

# Agent roles

**Status:** permission envelopes for work in this ecosystem, 2026-11-18.
**Precedence:** `AGENTS.md` → `docs/DECISION-LOG.md` entries → this file. A conflict
resolves upward, and this file is corrected in the same change.
**Authorises nothing.** A role bounds *how* an authorised item is executed; the
authorisation is an `IA-n` in the decision log, and it is per item.

## 1. A role is not an identity

Several agents may hold one role; one agent may hold a role for one task and never again.
No agent accumulates roles, no role is a rank, and no role carries standing authority
between tasks. What authorises work is the `IA-n`, not the role — which is why an agent
cannot bootstrap permission by naming itself.

## 2. The four roles

### `contract-steward`

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **May** | edit `docs/AA-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT.md` strictly within a stated `IA`; clarify wording; add a revision row |
| **May not** | touch `src/`, `public/`, `wrangler.jsonc`, `evidence/`; change an invariant; bump the wire version without an `IA` that says so; promote or demote a conformance level |
| **Must produce** | the revision-table row, the `IA-n` it relied on, the list of every section touched, and confirmation that no other section changed |

### `mind-implementer`

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **May** | edit `src/`, `public/`, `test.mjs`; add tests; run `npm run check`, `npm test`, `npm run build`; start a dev server for preview |
| **May not** | change `wrangler.jsonc`, `migrations`, bindings, or secrets; deploy; push to `main`; alter a stored KV record |
| **Must produce** | the actual output of each check run, the files changed, and an explicit list of what was **not** verified |

### `ara-observer`

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **May** | issue `GET` requests to the Cloudflare API **with a read-only credential**; read the deployed bundle and settings; quote probe results |
| **May not** | send any `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE`; use a credential that is parked or unverified (`OD-8`); treat a client's assumptions as ARA's specification; infer quality from shape |
| **Must produce** | `evidence/<component>-<date>/` with a `README.md` stating method, what the evidence supports, what it does not establish, and redaction status; and a correction to contract §9 wherever reality differs |

### `evidence-verifier`

| | |
| --- | --- |
| **May** | read everything, including other agents' claims and evidence |
| **May not** | write source or documentation; amend someone else's evidence; accept a claim because it is well written |
| **Must produce** | a verdict per connection — the level earned under contract §7.1, the exact evidence relied on, and "not verified" wherever evidence is missing or uncommitted (§7.4) |

## 3. Stop and ask

Quoted from `AGENTS.md` §9, plus the ecosystem's own additions. Any of these ends the
task and returns a question, regardless of role:

1. The change is irreversible, or touches stored truth, KV or R2 contents.
2. It needs a deploy or a push to `main`.
3. It would create a worker, or change a binding or namespace.
4. A named model is unavailable, or a check fails for a reason the agent cannot explain.
5. Two instructions conflict, or an instruction file disagrees with the code.
6. **It would write to ARA** — including registering a domain or recording a decision.
7. **It would mint, widen or reuse an approval token.**
8. **It would use a credential the decision log has parked.**

## 4. Working conventions

- **One work item per chat and branch.** Branch is `freebuff/<chat-id>`; work that spans
  two components is two items with two `IA`s, not one branch.
- **A pull request body names five things:** the `IA-n` relied on; what changed; the
  checks run and their results; what was **not** verified; and the evidence path. A PR
  that omits any of the five is not ready for review.
- **Never commit, echo, or place a secret in a command line.** Load credentials through
  `read -s` and an environment variable, as `docs/TOKEN-ROTATION-RUNBOOK.md` does.
- **Report per `docs/NEXT-STEP-HANDOFF-PROTOCOL.md`** — six parts, one next step, one of
  three authority values.

## 5. What no role may do

Mint an approval. Claim conformance. Edit an `IA` entry. Extend its own scope. Act on a
parked decision. Speak for ARA's reasoning or for AA's mediation. Authorise anything —
including itself.

## 6. When two roles collide

The usual case: a contract revision implies a code change.

It is **two items**. The steward edits the contract under its own `IA` and stops; the
implementer changes `src/` under a separate `IA` and cites the revision it implements.
Neither may do the other's half "while they are in there", because that is exactly how a
document revision silently becomes a runtime change. Sequencing is recorded in the
decision log, not agreed in chat.

## 7. Roles and the future AA/ARA

Today these are conventions a reviewer checks against. When AA exists, part of the work
becomes machine-enforced: capability checks against a host's manifest, and approval
verification. That will not replace this file — it will enforce the subset that can be
expressed as data, and leave the reporting and evidence duties exactly where they are.

Until then, `A1`–`A9` are held by discipline. This file is what that discipline is
called when someone asks whether it was followed.

# Decision log

**Purpose:** the one record of what has been decided, observed, and authorised. If a
change is not authorised here, it is not authorised.

**The rule that makes this log worth keeping:** *a requirement is not an
authorisation.* An entry has exactly one type, and only one of the four types
permits anything to happen.

| Type | Means | Who may raise it | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OD** — operator decision | The owner decided something | the owner only | Binds the architecture. Supersedes earlier entries by reference |
| **AD** — architectural decision | A structural choice accepted as the design | the owner; recorded by an agent | Binds until superseded. Changing one is a new OD, not an edit |
| **OB** — observation | A measured fact about a running system | any agent, **with evidence** | Informs. Changes nothing by itself, however alarming |
| **IA** — implementation authorisation | Permission to change a repository, runtime, binding, secret or deployment | the owner only | Scoped and dated. Names exactly what may change and nothing else |

Numbering is permanent: `OD-n`, `AD-n`, `OB-n`, `IA-n`. An entry is never rewritten;
it is superseded by a later entry that names it. Observations without an evidence
path are not observations.

---

## Standing constraints

These hold without restating on every entry.

1. **No deploy without explicit authorisation; creating a worker also needs it.**
   A push to `main` *is* a deploy here (`.github/workflows/deploy.yml`).
2. **No production write credentials for agents.** Read-only must be enforced by the
   credential, not by instructions.
3. **Mind owns its runtime, data, permissions and execution.** AA holds no truth.
   ARA writes nothing into a host.
4. **No component may silently acquire another's authority.**
5. **The owner reviews and authorises consequential changes.** A merge is the
   authorisation for a deploy; a written approval is the authorisation for anything
   else.
6. **`docs/AA-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT.md` governs.** Its invariants are not redefined
   here or in a chat.

---

## Operator decisions

| # | Date | Decision |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **OD-1** | 2026-11-18 | Three components with separate authorities: **ARA** reasoning, **AA** interaction/integration, **Mind** host application. Mind integrates with AA and does not independently connect to or recreate ARA |
| **OD-2** | 2026-11-18 | `docs/AA-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT.md` is the governing specification. Its invariants and authority boundaries are not redefined independently |
| **OD-3** | 2026-11-18 | **Security priority.** Revoke or rotate the token exposed to the agent environment; create a dedicated inspection token with verified read-only permissions; keep deployment credentials exclusively in GitHub Actions secrets; never give a Freebuff agent production write authority |
| **OD-4** | 2026-11-18 | **AA becomes an independent service**, in stages: contract → implemented and verified inside Mind → independent AA service → Mind switches from the in-process adapter to the service binding → a second application proves portability. The destination is approved architecturally; **creating the worker still needs explicit implementation approval** |
| **OD-5** | 2026-11-18 | This log distinguishes operator decisions, architectural decisions, observations and implementation authorisations. **Recording a requirement must not accidentally authorise its implementation** |
| **OD-6** | 2026-11-18 | **A1 and ARA's public surface are separate controls.** A1 governs the host→AA→ARA integration boundary. ARA's unauthenticated routes are a security defect in ARA. Routing all future traffic through AA does not secure ARA while those endpoints remain public |
| **OD-7** | 2026-11-18 | Documentation foundation before implementation: `ECOSYSTEM.md` and `AGENT-ROLES.md` proceed after scope review; `DECISION-LOG.md` and the contract §7.4 amendment proceed now; the `aa-integration-review` skill is **deferred** until the written standard is settled |
| **OD-8** | 2026-11-18 | The token-management `401` does **not** establish that the existing token lacks other permissions. Treat the existing agent token as **potentially compromised until it is revoked**, and verify the GitHub deployment credential's minimum required permissions rather than assuming `Workers Scripts:Edit` is sufficient or minimal |
| **OD-9** | 2026-11-18 | **AD-7 is qualified.** Merge to `main` is *a* production gate today, not *the* gate: two publishers deploy on push (OB-7). Describing it as the sole production gate — and therefore as the sole authorisation for a deploy — becomes honest only once the second publisher is reconciled |

---

## Architectural decisions

| # | Date | Decision | Governed by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **AD-1** | 2026-11-18 | **One direction of integration:** hosts integrate with AA; AA integrates with ARA. No host binds ARA, and no host reimplements it | Contract A1 |
| **AD-2** | 2026-11-18 | **The contract is data plus nine invariants** (A1–A9): an eight-connection manifest, a versioned envelope, and a boundary law that a change is rejected against | Contract §0–§3 |
| **AD-3** | 2026-11-18 | **A manifest is not evidence.** Four conformance levels (`declared → implemented → verified → conforming`); the aggregate is the lowest connection; no promotion from documentation or static tests | Contract §7 |
| **AD-4** | 2026-11-18 | **Provenance cannot be upgraded in transit.** No layer sets `verified: true` on evidence it did not originate and verify; a correlation id is never provenance | Contract A6, §5 |
| **AD-5** | 2026-11-18 | **Explicit approval requires an authenticated actor**, and `execute` capabilities fail closed when there is nobody to name. The anonymous `override` path stays documented legacy and is not extended | Contract A9, §4.3 |
| **AD-6** | 2026-11-18 | **One repository (`mind`) is the ecosystem authority until AA has a runtime.** Splitting `aa` and `aa-contract` out is correct *after* AA exists as a service, because cross-repo change cannot be atomic and the contract is not yet implemented | `AGENTS.md` §1; OD-4 |
| **AD-7** | 2026-11-18 | **Freebuff is the development and orchestration environment, never a fourth authority.** It holds branches, documents and shells. Its only path to production is a merge the owner performs, which CI turns into a deploy | OD-1, OD-3 |

---

## Observations

Every entry names its evidence. None of these changes anything by itself.

| # | Date | Observation | Evidence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **OB-1** | 2026-11-18 | The deployed `ara` worker is a 67,876-byte module (2,040 lines), last modified **2026-11-18 04:17:36 UTC**, compatibility date 2025-07-01, reasoning on OpenRouter, with no `AI` binding | `evidence/ara-discovery/` (`ara.worker.mjs`, `bindings.json`, `README.md`) |
| **OB-2** | 2026-11-18 | **A2 holds at runtime.** ARA holds a `MIND` service binding and references it **zero times**, so nothing in ARA writes into Mind | `evidence/ara-discovery/`, token scan |
| **OB-3** | 2026-11-18 | ARA tracks exactly one domain (`general`) and collapses any unregistered domain to it, so Mind's hardcoded `domain: 'mind'` is discarded. `surface: 'mind'` is load-bearing and selects ARA's mind face | `GET /domains` probe; bundle `arrive()` |
| **OB-4** | 2026-11-18 | Five routes answer unauthenticated from the public internet: `POST /decide`, `POST /resolve`, `GET /domains`, `GET /review`, `GET /progress`. `/resolve` runs a generation path on the owner's OpenRouter key; `/domains` publishes a 364-decision histogram | router source; live probes |
| **OB-5** | 2026-11-18 | Mind discards ARA's returned `notes`, so the learning round trip is one way; and Mind authenticates the journal with `ARA_KEY \|\| ADMIN_KEY` while ARA accepts only its own `ADMIN_KEY` — a likely 401 on every outcome and verdict if the two differ | `src/ara.js`; bundle `adminGate` |
| **OB-6** | 2026-11-18 | Two evidence directories named by existing docs are **absent** from this working tree, so the `verified` claims resting on them cannot be audited | `docs/SETUP-AS-BUILT.md`, `docs/JUSTICE-ECOSYSTEM-BASELINE.md`, `ls evidence/` |
| **OB-7** | 2026-11-18 | A push to `main` reaches production twice: a Cloudflare Builds integration and the workflow both deploy | `HANDOFF.md` §10 |
| **OB-8** | 2026-11-18 | The agent environment held an account-scoped Cloudflare token with at least Workers Scripts **read**. Value never printed and only `GET`s were issued, but the placement itself is the finding OD-3 answers | this session |
| **OB-9** | 2026-11-18 | `ara` has no source repository in the account or on GitHub under that name, so the deployed bundle is the only copy of its code | `PROJECTS.md`; bundle pull |
| **OB-10** | 2026-11-18 | **Neither credential's real scope is established.** This session's `401` on `/user/tokens/verify` proves one missing scope, not a bounded token. And `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` states `Workers Scripts:Edit` in a **comment**; that is a claim, not a verified minimum | workflow comment; this session |

---

## Implementation authorisations

**Runtime authorisations so far: none.** No entry in this log permits a change to a
binding, a secret, a deployment, a Worker, or any ARA state.

| # | Date | Scope | Type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |

| **IA-7** | 2026-11-18 | Create `docs/TOKEN-ROTATION-RUNBOOK.md`: owner steps for revoking the exposed token, issuing a single-permission read-only inspection token, proving it with three read probes and one non-destructive deny probe, and recording the result as an observation. It performs no rotation and touches no credential | documentation only |
| **IA-8** | 2026-11-18 | Create `docs/ECOSYSTEM.md` (components, authority, edges, deployment gates with the two-publisher qualification, staged path to AA, and what AA and ARA still need before a second host) and `docs/AGENT-ROLES.md` (four role briefs, stop-and-ask triggers, PR conventions). Documentation only: no runtime, binding, secret, credential use or deploy | documentation only |

| Item | Needs from the owner |

## Adding an entry

1. Pick the type. If it would authorise work, it is an **IA** and only the owner

# Ecosystem — ARA, AA, Mind

**Status:** describes the architecture as intended and as it stands, 2026-11-18.
**Authorises nothing.** Authorisation lives in `docs/DECISION-LOG.md`; the integration
itself is governed by `docs/AA-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT.md`; the rules that bind agents are
`AGENTS.md`.
**Not:** a rulebook, a plan with approvals attached, or a conformance claim.

## 1. The three components

| Component | Authority | Runtime | Exists today |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **ARA** | Reasoning: intent, domains, decisions, confidence, learning | Worker `ara` | Deployed 2026-11-18 04:17 UTC; **no repository**; interface recorded in contract §9 |
| **AA** | Mediation: envelope, capabilities, context, the ARA gateway | **None** | Specification only — contract rev 1.2, wire `aa-contract/1` |
| **Mind** | Operational: bindings, store, deployment, approval | Worker `mind` + repo | Deployed; **binds ARA directly**; below `declared` |

Two sentences carry the whole design. **Hosts integrate with AA; AA integrates with
ARA** (`A1`). **Authority follows the OD/AD entries, not the agent that happens to be
working.**

## 2. The governing arrangement

```text
   you ── direction · corrections · decisions · authorisation
    │
    ▼
 Freebuff ── repo work · specialised agents · tests · evidence · pull requests
    │
    ├── branch / PR ──▶ your merge ──▶ CI (npm ci · test · build · wrangler deploy)
    │                                        │
    │                                        ▼                    runtime
    │                                   worker `mind`  ──────▶  ARA · AA
    └── never in the runtime path
```

Freebuff holds branches, documents and shells. Its only route to production is a merge
the owner performs, which CI turns into a deploy. It is therefore an orchestration
environment and not a fourth authority — not by policy, but by topology.

`OD-3` adds the other half: **no agent holds production write authority.** The deploy
credential is a GitHub Actions secret; the agent credential is read-only, and currently
parked pending rotation (`OD-8`).

## 3. The three edges

| Edge | Carries | Governed by | Exists? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| host → AA | envelope: identity, intent, domain, context with provenance, capabilities, approval | contract §2.1, §3 | **No** |
| AA → ARA | the same envelope plus AA's validation | contract §1, §2 | **No** |
| ARA → host, via AA | decision, `authority` (`writes: []`), provenance, notes | `A2`, contract §2.2 | **No** — Mind calls ARA directly |
| operator → host → AA → ARA | verdict, correction, preference, each with its actor | contract §6, R-F1 | Partial — Mind sends verdicts, but only after ARA accepts them (`OB-5`) |

Read the third row and the fourth together: every edge in the intended architecture is
currently absent or partial. That is not a criticism of the work; it is the honest
scoreboard, and it is why the first proof is not "AA exists" but "Mind cannot reach ARA
without it".

## 4. Is this a component?

A component is a **runtime**, an **edge** into it, and **committed evidence** that the
edge is enforced (contract §7.4). An agent, a document or a diagram is none of those.

| | Runtime | Edge | Evidence | Verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ARA | yes | Mind → ARA, direct | `evidence/ara-discovery/` | a **dependency**, not yet an integrated service |
| AA | no | none | the contract itself | a **specification** |
| Mind | yes | direct to ARA | build + test green, no exchanges | an **application** that has not integrated |

## 5. What actually gates production

| Gate | Requires | Who |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Code change | branch + PR | any role |
| Deploy | **merge to `main`** | owner |
| Binding change | explicit authorisation — a deploy re-declares bindings, so this is a production change | owner |
| New worker | explicit authorisation **and** an exception to `AGENTS.md` §2.3 | owner |
| Secret change | owner action | owner |
| Wire-version bump of the contract | authorisation, recorded as a revision | owner |
| Any write into ARA | explicit authorisation | owner |

**One qualification, and it must stay visible:** merge to `main` is *a* production gate,
not *the* gate. Two publishers deploy on push (`OB-7`): the workflow, and a Cloudflare
Builds integration that is invisible from this repository. Until that is reconciled
(`OD-9`), no document or agent may describe merge as the sole production gate — doing so
would assert a control the system does not have.

## 6. The path to AA as a service (`OD-4`)

| Stage | What it establishes | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | the contract | done — rev 1.2 |
| 2 | the contract implemented **inside Mind**, labelled `adapter: in-process` | authorisation (`IA`); capped at `verified` by §7.2 rule 4 |
| 3 | the independent `aa` service | **explicit authorisation**, plus an exception to `AGENTS.md` §2.3 |
| 4 | Mind replaces the adapter with the service binding, and **loses `env.ARA`** | authorisation: a binding removal |
| 5 | a second application connects, without editing AA | proof the standard is real |

Stage 4 is the one that matters and the one easiest to defer: as long as Mind keeps a
direct ARA binding, stages 1–3 are additive and change nothing load-bearing.

## 7. What AA and ARA still need before a second host

Neither list is a wish; each item is something whose absence makes portability false.

**AA**

| Need | Why it is structural | Today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a runtime | otherwise "AA integrates with ARA" is a diagram | none |
| to be the only holder of the ARA binding | `A1` is true when Mind *loses* `env.ARA`, not when it gains a path | Mind binds ARA directly |
| a manifest registry per host, versioned | capability enforcement needs something to enforce | no manifests exist |
| an approval-verification scheme | §4.2 has the host mint tokens; §4.3 has AA refuse unapproved execution. A service cannot verify what it did not mint, and the contract does not say how it would | **spec gap** |
| a subject identity that is not a host session | AA must know which operator it accompanies without holding a host's Durable Object | per-host `SESSIONS` |
| a degradation rule | AA unreachable ⇒ hosts fail closed for reasoning, or the direct seam returns | unstated |
| end-to-end correlation and an evidence sink | §7 needs records that tie a host request to an ARA decision | ARA returns only its own `id` |
| an owner, a release process, a deprecation policy | a shared layer that changes silently is a second source of drift | no owner, because no runtime |

**ARA**

| Need | Why it is structural | Today |
| --- | --- | --- |
| a source repository | the deployed bundle is the only copy; nothing below can be reviewed or implemented without it | `OB-9` |
| a closed surface | "AA is the only caller" is meaningless while five routes answer the internet | `OB-4` |
| the envelope, in and out | `contract`, `identity`, `authority.writes: []`, `provenance` | none of them |
| surfaces as data | `SURFACES` is hardcoded to `mind` and `cards`; a third host needs a code change — **ARA's portability blocker** | hardcoded |
| a loud domain policy | silent collapse to `general` teaches a host that it registered knowledge it did not | `OB-3` |
| per-caller keys | one `ADMIN_KEY` also opens its console, and may not match Mind's `ARA_KEY` | `OB-5` |
| retention and PII policy | the reasoning authority accumulates operator behaviour with no stated lifetime | unstated |
| binding hygiene | `MIND`, `CODS`, `MASTER_TRUTHS`, `BROWSER`, `R2` bound and unused; a binding into a host is an authority channel | `OB-2` |
| a move-set deprecation policy | `result/preset/ask/unclear` is the *mind* vocabulary; changing it silently breaks hosts | unstated |

**What neither may acquire:** a host's store, approval authority, truth, deploy rights
over a host, or any need to know that Mind exists. Growth in that direction is how a
three-part architecture becomes a monolith with three names.

**The graduation test** is two observations, not a milestone list: ARA serves a second
host with **zero change to ARA's source**; and Mind **stops reasoning when AA does**, and
says so.

## 8. Where each fact lives

| Artifact | Owns | Must not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AGENTS.md` | the rules that bind agents, and the ecosystem hierarchy | hold open questions or drifting counts |
| `docs/AA-INTEGRATION-CONTRACT.md` | invariants, envelope, capabilities, conformance | authorise work, or describe a running system's quality |
| `docs/DECISION-LOG.md` | decisions, observations, authorisations | host the contract's rules |
| `docs/NEXT-STEP-HANDOFF-PROTOCOL.md` | how a response ends | grant authority |
| `docs/TOKEN-ROTATION-RUNBOOK.md` | the owner's credential steps | perform them |
| `evidence/<component>-<date>/` | what was measured, and what it does not establish | carry secrets |
| `PROJECTS.md` | the generated inventory | be edited by hand |

## 9. Structural risks — pointers only

`OB-7` two publishers; `OB-4` ARA's public routes; `OB-6` evidence that documents name
but the tree lacks; `OB-5` discarded notes and a possibly mismatched journal key;
`OB-10` neither credential's scope verified; and the §4.2/§4.3 approval-verification gap
in §7 above. Each is recorded where it can be checked, not here.

## 10. What this document does not do

It does not restate the invariants, define a capability, authorise a stage, claim
conformance, or describe merge as the sole production gate. It records relationships
and boundaries; the evidence decides the rest.

files.text:
# EZ EXHIBITZ — owner entitlement

Status: **instructed**, not implemented, not verified. Written by `mind` under
`docs/MIND-AUTHORITY.md`. The `ezxhibitz` source is not in this repository, so every
claim about the existing gate below is a requirement, not an observation.

## 1. What is being asked for

A permanent owner entitlement that survives IP changes, browser changes and the
ordinary restrictions applied to customers, and that is separate from Founder and
Professional access. It must be validated server-side from a credential. Recognition
by IP address, user-agent or any other attribute of the connection is not acceptable:
those fail on a new network or a new laptop, and they are guessable by anyone who can
see one of the owner's requests.

## 2. Two axes, kept apart

| axis | values | what it governs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `role` | `customer`, `owner` | authority |
| `plan` | `free`, `founder`, `professional` | the commercial tier |

Owner is a role, not a high plan. Keep the axes separate so a plan change never
grants authority, and so the checks read one capability table. If the gate as
deployed already has a single decision function, the role belongs inside it rather
than beside it.

Owner is also not admin. Entitlement buys gated features for the owner's own use; it
does not let the owner read or write another customer's records. Those stay behind
whatever admin credential already guards them, unchanged.

## 3. The credential

Two Worker secrets, both set by the owner with `wrangler secret put`, neither ever
written into a file, a command, a commit, a chat or client code:

- `OWNER_ACCESS_CODE` — the code itself. At least 32 bytes of entropy, generated by
  the owner (base32 or hex). Never transmitted after the exchange in §4.
- `OWNER_SESSION_KEY` — the HMAC key used to sign sessions. Separate from the code so
  that sessions can be invalidated without changing it.

The code is presented in a request header, never in a query string, path segment or
fragment, so it cannot reach referrers, proxy logs or access logs. Compare it in
constant time — hash both sides and compare the digests, or compare equal-length
buffers with `crypto.timingSafeEqual` — after normalising to avoid length leaks.

A wrong code gets one generic `401` with no body beyond a stable error code. Never
reveal whether a code exists, how close it was, or whether owner access is configured
at all. Rate-limit attempts per source (for example five per minute) with backoff, and
keep that limiter active for the owner path too.

## 4. Session exchange

The code is exchanged once for a session, so it crosses the wire approximately never.

`POST /api/owner/session` — the name is provisional; map it onto the gate's own
routing convention — takes the code in the header, verifies it, and sets a cookie:

- `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`, `Path=/`, `Max-Age` no longer than 30 days;
- value is a signed claim `{ role: "owner", v: 1, exp }`, HMAC-signed with
  `OWNER_SESSION_KEY`;
- nothing in the claim or the cookie is bound to an IP address, a user-agent, a
  browser fingerprint or a device id.

Every later request verifies the signature and the expiry only. That is what makes it
survive travelling, switching networks and changing browsers; the code is the recovery
path in a browser with no valid session. A companion route that clears the cookie is
fine but not required.

## 5. Where the decision is made

One place. Find the single point where the existing gate decides whether a request may
proceed, and make the role part of that decision. Do not add a second parallel check,
and do not special-case owner inside individual features.

The client may render an owner badge from the session, but the client never decides
entitlement. No request is ever trusted because it claims a role.

## 6. What owner may bypass, and what it must not

May bypass, for the owner's own use — commercial restrictions:

- the paywall and the packet limit;
- per-day quotas and seat limits;
- demo and content-creation limits;
- export or watermark restrictions on content the owner created.

Must not bypass, ever — security controls:

- authentication or authorisation of any other user;
- admin-key gates on destructive routes;
- rate limits and abuse ceilings;
- audit logging — owner actions are logged, under a distinct actor, so the owner's
  traffic is separable from customers';
- per-customer data isolation;
- legal or contract gates that apply to everyone.

Owner usage gets its own counters rather than an exemption from counting, so a leaked
code shows up as anomalous usage instead of invisible usage.

## 7. Prohibited implementations

- the code in a query string, path or fragment;
- the code in `localStorage`, `sessionStorage`, IndexedDB or a URL the user can share;
- the code compiled into the client bundle, a build constant or an HTML attribute;
- entitlement derived from a body field, a header or a stored flag the client controls;
- logging the code or the session token;
- an IP allowlist or user-agent match standing in for the credential;
- writing `owner` onto a customer record as a plan;
- a per-feature bypass instead of the single gate.

## 8. Rotation and revocation

- New code: replace `OWNER_ACCESS_CODE`. Existing sessions continue until they expire.
- Invalidate every session at once: rotate `OWNER_SESSION_KEY`.
- Invalidate every session without touching either secret: bump the version claim and
  reject anything below the current value.

Revocation must be immediate and global; there is no per-device registry to clean up.

## 9. Acceptance tests

A change is not done until these pass against the running worker, with the negative
cases included:

1. No credential → `401`, no cookie, no detail about whether owner access exists.
2. Wrong code → `401`, generic code, no cookie; repeated attempts are rate-limited.
3. Right code → session cookie set, with `HttpOnly`, `Secure`, `SameSite=Lax`.
4. Request with the session → the specific gated feature opens, named explicitly in
   the test.
5. Tampered signature → `401`, no capability.
6. Expired session, and a session below the current version → `401`.
7. Code in a query string → not honoured.
8. A customer gains nothing: no header, a forged `role=owner` body field, a forged
   storage flag, a replayed cookie from another account.
9. Founder and Professional behaviour is unchanged — their existing tests still pass,
   unmodified.
10. The owner cannot read or write another customer's records.
11. Owner actions appear in the audit log under a distinct actor.

## 10. Reporting status

Per `docs/MIND-AUTHORITY.md`, the status is one of three:

- **instructed** — this document exists (it does, now);
- **implemented** — the `ezxhibitz` source contains the role, the constant-time
  comparison, the signed session and the single-gate decision, with the tests above;
- **conforming** — the deployed worker has been exercised and behaves as §9 describes.

The first implementation step is a read-only inventory of the gate: its route names,
its storage, its tier vocabulary (Founder, Professional), where it currently decides
access, and whether that is one choke point or several. This document deliberately
does not guess any of those.
